BLD-artifact_numbering.content:
The numbered artifacts SHALL follow this scheme:

```text
0X  workspace infrastructure (phase-neutral): config, guard, live database
1X  prep-phase artifacts        (currently: 10 = prep plan, 11 = handoff, 15 = prep audit log + prep DB snapshot)
2X  geotag-phase artifacts        (currently: 21–26; 26 = complete log + geotag DB snapshot + archive manifest)
3X  merge-phase artifacts        (currently: 30 = merge plan, 31 = merge summary, 35 = merge log + merge DB snapshot + archive manifest)
```

The first digit SHALL mean only the producing phase. The second SHALL be a sequence number within the phase with no
further meaning: an absent number is not reserved, not headroom and not missing, and nothing is to be inferred from a
gap. Sibling end-of-phase records that differ only by extension MAY share a number — `photos-15-prep-log.json` and
`photos-15-prep-ingest.db` are both the end-of-prep record, one the human-readable log and one the database image;
likewise `photos-26-complete-log.json`, `photos-26-geotag-ingest.db` and `photos-26-archive-manifest.json`, and the
three `photos-35` files. The full filename — number, name and
extension — SHALL be the identifier, never the number alone; `photos-0X-*` (and `1X`, `2X`, `3X`) names a band. The
bands are unrelated to the numbered media folders `0-sources`…`6-photos-by-dest`.

BLD-decision_records.content:
The decisions SHALL live in the `user_decision` fields of geotag's `photos-21`, `photos-22` and `photos-23`, each field
created by geotag and preserved across regeneration (geotag §9, §20); the decision editor SHALL write only those
fields. A change SHALL be traced from its decision record through the `depends_on` fingerprints (§9) to the executable
plan and the run's journal (prep §14.3; geotag §4–§6, §29). Merge takes no decision; its placement is a fixed rule over
recorded inputs, recorded the same way (merge §8–§9). Every plan SHALL decide about a photo from its own values, pinned
before geotag first wrote to it (geotag §24.2), so a withdrawn manual position is undone like any decision: the photo is
placed again, or geotag's position cleared; an automatic position is recomputed, never rolled back.

BLD-idempotency.content:
Prep SHALL reuse the cached fingerprint and metadata of a file whose size and modification time are unchanged, and
carry a moved file's identity forward without reading it (prep §10, §13); a plan never executed SHALL leave its
fingerprints and metadata for the next plan to reuse (prep §10.3). Geotag SHALL reuse its resolved-UTC cache while its
inputs are unchanged and keep each decision whose target is unchanged (geotag §9, §22.1). Fingerprinting (ImageMagick
`identify`, `ffmpeg`), metadata extraction (`exiftool`) and GPX parsing SHALL run only for new or changed inputs.
Staleness SHALL follow the field-scoped fingerprints of the dependency cascade (§9). A file's operation SHALL be planned
only where the file does not already hold the target: prep does not move or rename a file already in place, geotag
plans no write a file already holds and recomputes an already-final name to itself (geotag §27, §28.2), and merge
records a photo already in the library as already present (merge §7). A run's summary SHALL count the cache hits and
the files already right. Each phase's own consequences are in its spec: prep §13 and §21, geotag §29.1 and §30, merge
§8.

BLD-log_format.content:
Each log SHALL be pretty-printed JSON with sorted keys, its `photos` keyed by the content fingerprint (`content_fingerprint`),
each entry carrying where each phase left the photo — `prep_path`, written by prep and updated by every prep run;
`geotag_path`, by finalize, its by-dest folder under the name its last final rename gave it; `library_path`, by merge —
and a `journey` of steps, each step naming its `phase` and `action`, a move or rename
its `from` and `to` — the first step's `from` being the photo's path in the dump — and, where a decision caused it, a
`because` naming the decision exactly: a clock offset its `photos-21` cell, with its day where the camera's photos
there span days (`camera_group_time_decisions.<group>@<date>`), or the `photos-22` drift confirmation whose validated
offset replaced it; a timezone its destination's cell; a manual position the photo's pin among `photos-23`'s review
items or the destination's folder fallback, with the destination it was accepted from. Geotag's steps SHALL be
`clock_offset_applied` (its `offset_seconds` with an `offset_description` in words, such as "camera clock 1 h 55 min
ahead of UTC"), `resolved_utc`, `timezone_resolved`, `time_written`, `gps_written` (with its origin, method and,
for a manual position, the position it replaced, from the plan), `gps_cleared` (a position geotag wrote
and no longer places, with that position, from the plan, and the method left), `gps_preserved` and `final_rename`,
each naming its `run`;
finalize SHALL take them from every executed pass — each superseded `photos-24` whose journal shows it ran, oldest
first, matched by fingerprint — before the current plan's, from the provenance each time write carries (geotag §31). Each run's journal SHALL be kept as
its own `journal-<run>.json`, and each geotag execution SHALL keep the decision records its plan depended on, verified
by hash, in `executed/<plan id>/`, which a step's `because_record` and `because_record_sha256` name; prep marks its log partial and warns when its history cannot rebuild a journey (prep
§16.1); geotag's finalize marks `partial` the entry of a photo carrying geotag's mark whose own values the workspace
never pinned, with a `history_incomplete` step of its own saying why, and names in the log's `warnings`, the log then `partial`, any pass whose journal is kept
but whose plan is missing (geotag §31).

BLD-loop_commands.content:
The loop SHALL run as: `prep plan`, `dry-run`, `execute`; the sort, by hand; the prep commands again; `geotag plan`, the
decision editor (`edit`) for what it asks, and `geotag plan` again until `photos-24-executable-plan.json` is ready;
`geotag execute`, which writes `photos-25-execution-summary.json`; `geotag finalize`, which writes
`photos-26-complete-log.json` and the archival package; and `merge plan`, `dry-run`, `execute`. When the only change
prep has not recorded is a sort and the inbox is empty, `geotag plan` SHALL run prep's `plan` and `execute` itself,
saying so, before it plans.

(merge §3). A development subfolder SHALL be one named in `destination_distribution_subfolders`.

there, merge SHALL fingerprint it — from `library_fingerprint_cache` when its path, size and modification time match a
row, otherwise by decoding it and adding the row — and compare it with the incoming photo's fingerprint from prep. An
incoming photo whose name is taken by different content SHALL take the shared suffix convention's next free suffix
(§7.2), the library's own name keeping its bare form.

BLD-phase_logs.content:
Prep SHALL write `photos-15-prep-log.json` at the end of every prep run (prep §16.1). Geotag's finalize SHALL copy it
to `photos-26-complete-log.json` and append each photo's geotag steps (§13.3); merge SHALL copy that to
`photos-35-merge-log.json` and append its own (§13.5). Each copy SHALL carry the earlier log unchanged — every entry,
every field and every step as it was, a phase only adding — and finalize and merge SHALL check it: a copy that would
change the earlier record is not written, and merge SHALL refuse while `photos-26-complete-log.json` no longer carries
`photos-15-prep-log.json` so, or cannot be read. A prep log missing or unreadable at finalize SHALL be named in the
complete log's `warnings`, the log then `partial`. Each phase's job records — prep's handoff and summary, geotag's
decision, plan and execution-summary records, merge's summary — SHALL stay on disk, as SHALL every pass's plan and
journal and the decision records each execution kept (`BLD-log_format`).

BLD-plan_backups.content:
A differing re-plan SHALL first rename the existing artifact under the shared incremental `-NNN` suffix (shared §7.2) —
`photos-10-prep-plan-001.json`, say — and announce where; byte-identical content SHALL write nothing and back up
nothing. A plan carrying a fresh plan id differs every run, so re-planning it always preserves the prior plan. The
per-run journals SHALL keep their `journal-<run_id>.json` naming; this convention governs the plan and decision
artifacts.

BLD-prep_guards_with_the_whole_hash.content:
Prep SHALL re-plan from the filesystem each run and guard execution with the whole-file hash; it SHALL keep no folder
or extension fingerprint of its own.
BLD-prep_guards_with_the_whole_hash.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace

BLD-prep_skip_set.content:
Prep SHALL skip `.photos-ingest/`, `.photos-ingest-quarantine/` and `.git` as whole subtrees, every dot-prefixed file,
and the strays folder `1-strays/` with all its `<plan-id>` subfolders (prep §3, §3.2). The strays of a run SHALL go to
`1-strays/<plan-id>/`. Hidden dotfiles in a dump area SHALL be swept to the quarantine (prep §3, §15).
BLD-prep_skip_set.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media

BLD-prep_skip_set.title: What prep skips

BLD-record_ownership.content:
A phase SHALL write only records in its own number band of the numbering scheme: prep `photos-1X`, geotag `photos-2X`,
merge `photos-3X`. The configuration and the database are phase-neutral, each with its own writers' rule: prep seeds
the configuration, which `init-library` may later extend by `library_root` alone (§4), and prep writes the database's
cache and identity rows while geotag and merge write only their own regions of it (§13.4). Bundling copies of every phase's records into the archival package reads them, and is no write.
BLD-record_ownership.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-record_ownership.title: Which phase writes which record

BLD-rerun_recognition.content:
Geotag SHALL record what it wrote in the file's `GPSProcessingMethod`: the bare value `interpolated`, `manual_locked`
or `manual_fallback` beside each position it writes, and, when it fixes the time and writes no position, the suffix
`+carto-time` appended once to whatever the field held, keeping the device's own value. Any other value is the
device's own, and the GPS beside it native. Before geotag's first write to a file, execution SHALL pin its own time, offset tag, position and
`GPSProcessingMethod` in an original-values ledger keyed by fingerprint, once, unless it already carries geotag's mark;
a later plan SHALL decide about a pinned file from those values and plan only the writes that differ from what it
holds (geotag §24.2). On a re-run, a file with no pinned values carrying a position marker or the suffix SHALL be
resolved from its own time and offset tag with no clock offset, SHALL be no clock anchor and in no drift check, and a
camera group's offset cells SHALL be built from its unmarked files alone. A file with a position marker SHALL count as
having no native GPS and be placed again; one now placed nowhere has geotag's position and marker cleared and carries
the suffix alone. A write SHALL be planned only where the file does not already hold its value, and names are
recomputed from the destination's local time, a file already so named getting no rename (geotag §27, §28.2).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-rerun_recognition.title: How a re-run recognises what is settled

BLD-seal_marker.content:
The seal SHALL be `photos-00-sealed.json` in the control directory, its own file beside the workspace guard — which
only prep writes — recording `sealed`, the merge run id (`merged_run_id`) and `library_root`; its presence alone seals.
Prep's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute`, every geotag command, and merge's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` SHALL check it under the workspace
lock before reading anything else, and stop with exit status 2 if it is there, adding the likely-new-dump warning when
the workspace's top level holds a file or the inbox holds anything. `edit` SHALL refuse to serve a sealed workspace,
and its save SHALL write nothing there. `merge init-library` given a path from inside a workspace, which would record it
as `library_root` in the configuration, SHALL check the seal under the lock the same way, and stop with exit status 2
having blessed nothing; without a path, or from outside any workspace, it writes nothing in the workspace and does not
check. `prune-quarantine` SHALL not check the seal.
BLD-seal_marker.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed

BLD-seal_marker.title: The seal and its checks

sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media

BLD-shape_guards_by_phase.title: Where each phase applies the shape guards

BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.content:
The snapshot SHALL be a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block of the workspace configuration,
`photos-00-config.json`; with no `zfs` block, or one not enabled, none is taken. Its name SHALL carry the plan id.
`snapshots_required` decides what a failed snapshot means: true, the run aborts before its first change; false, or the
block not configured, it proceeds without one.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.title: The snapshot is a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block

BLD-top_level_entries.content:
The top level of an initialized workspace SHALL hold exactly the managed folders `0-sources`…`6-photos-by-dest` and
`.photos-ingest/`, `.photos-ingest-quarantine/`, `.git` and other dotfiles and dot-directories; the inbox SHALL be
`0-sources/`. Prep applies the guard (prep §3.1), geotag at startup (geotag §13), merge as its precondition 0a (merge
§3).
BLD-top_level_entries.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media

BLD-top_level_entries.title: The workspace's top level

BLD-track_file.content:
A track file SHALL be a file named `*.gpx`, `*.kml`, `*.kmz`, `*.fit`, `*.tcx`, `*.nmea` or `*.igc`, in any case. Of these geotag reads
only the `*.gpx` files beneath `gpx_root`. Prep SHALL raise one blocker for each it inventories, naming it, and leave it
out of the plan (prep §3, §6.1); and execute SHALL raise the same blocker for one that appeared after planning (prep
§14.3).
BLD-track_file.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-track_file.title: A track file

BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.content:
The whole-file fingerprint SHALL be carried in the `depends_on` of geotag's executable plan (geotag §28, in the
flattened dependency set of geotag §5) and of merge's plan, `config_fingerprint`, and each SHALL be refused when it no
longer matches the file. The costly caches SHALL be keyed on their own areas instead: resolved UTC on the
time-policy subset (geotag §22.1), the renames on the filename-format fingerprint.
BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.title: The whole-file hash is in the executable plan's dependencies

BLD-workspace_database.content:
The workspace database SHALL be SQLite, `photos-00-ingest.db` in `.photos-ingest/`. Its writers SHALL be: prep, of the
file and metadata caches (`file_cache`, `metadata_cache`) and their version row (`meta`), through its single-writer
path (prep §14.3); geotag, of the resolved-UTC cache (`resolved_utc_cache`), the values each photo held before geotag
first wrote to it (`original_values`, geotag §24.2); merge, of the library-file fingerprint cache (`library_fingerprint_cache`, keyed by the library file's absolute
path with its size and modification time). Where each photo landed is in merge's JSON records, not the database. Prep's
plan-time decode memo, `photos-00-plan-memo.db`, is the one other database: scratch, re-derivable, deletable at any
time (prep §10.3).

The images SHALL be `photos-15-prep-ingest.db`, written when prep writes its handoff and log; `photos-26-geotag-ingest.db`,
written by finalize with the complete log; and `photos-35-merge-ingest.db`, written when merge succeeds, before it
re-seals. Each SHALL be captured under the workspace lock by `VACUUM INTO` a `.tmp-` name in the control directory,
checked with `PRAGMA quick_check`, then renamed over the phase's earlier image.
BLD-workspace_database.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_database.title: The database: its file, its writers, its images

CHC-ask_only_what_data_cannot_settle.content: Resolve everything derivable automatically; ask only real judgment questions, and make each one cheap to answer.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-ask_only_what_data_cannot_settle.title: Ask only what the data can't settle

CHC-local_folder_library.content:
The destination is a plain directory tree on disk (feeds digiKam or Immich), not a cloud service or proprietary
catalog.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-local_folder_library.title: A local, owned, folder-based library

CHC-photos_matter.content: Because they matter, no original may be lost or silently altered — correctness beats convenience.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-photos_matter.title: Photos matter; they are irreplaceable, so they deserve care

CHC-total_placement.content:
Every photo ends up on the map — precise where tracks allow, rough or manual where they don't — so the result is a
*map-complete* library, not just the frames that came with a location.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-total_placement.title: 100% placement, even under GPS scarcity

DEF-archival_package.content:
The **archival package** is one archive, kept with the control records, holding the complete record of a dump's journey
through the pipeline — what was done to its photos and why. It is what the user keeps when the workspace goes away.
DEF-archival_package.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-archival_package.title: The archival package

DEF-camera_group.content:
A **camera group** is the photos one camera or device took, identified by a key derived from the device-identity
metadata the files carry.
DEF-camera_group.title: A camera group

DEF-config_areas.content:
The configuration sets, at least: the snapshot policy; which camera groups are phones and which have fixed clocks; the
filename timestamp format; where the tracks are and the thresholds for matching photos to them; the camera-time policy;
the library and how merge places files in it; the managed folders' names; and which extensions are which class of
media. Each area's detail is in the items of its own section.
DEF-config_areas.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
DEF-config_areas.title: What the configuration sets

DEF-configuration.content:
A workspace's **configuration** is the one record of the settings its runs read. It is kept in the workspace, beside
what is processed under it, and it is an input the user authors.
DEF-configuration.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
DEF-configuration.title: The configuration

DEF-control_records.content:
A workspace's **control records** are everything cartographer keeps in it besides the media: the configuration, the
plans and the decisions, the journals, the end-of-phase records and the databases.
DEF-control_records.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
DEF-control_records.title: The control records

DEF-database_image.content:
A phase's **database image** is a copy of the workspace database as it stood at the end of that phase's latest
successful run.
DEF-database_image.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-database_image.title: A phase's database image

DEF-decision.content:
A **decision** is a value the user records in one of geotag's records for the tool to act on — a destination's
timezone, an accepted time anchor, a clock offset, a confirmed drift check, a manual position, a folder fallback. The
tool *proposes*; the user *decides*.
DEF-decision.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
DEF-decision.title: A decision

DEF-dependency_cascade.content:
The **dependency cascade** is how the phases keep a record from being used once what it was made from has changed: each
record carries what it depends on — media by their fingerprints, other records by their hashes, and settings by the
fingerprints of the configuration areas it reads — and each use checks them first. Its full name, the
*dependency-fingerprint/hash cascade*, says that it tracks both kinds of identity.
DEF-dependency_cascade.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-dependency_cascade.title: The dependency cascade

DEF-development.content:
**Development** is the later processing of photos into distribution copies — the JPEG and TIFF breakout — kept in
subfolders of a destination.
DEF-development.title: Development

DEF-finalize.content:
**Finalize** is geotag's closing command, given once the user judges the workspace's media done: it assembles the
workspace's permanent record and its complete transformation log.
DEF-finalize.title: Finalize

DEF-fingerprint.content:
A media file's **fingerprint** is the identity of its decoded content — a photo's pixels, a video's streams. Unqualified,
*fingerprint* means this.
DEF-fingerprint.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-fingerprint.title: A fingerprint

DEF-geotag.content:
**Geotag**, the second phase, resolves each photo to its true time, inferring and correcting each camera's clock
offset; places the photos that carry no position along the recorded tracks; and renames each by its corrected local
time.
DEF-geotag.title: Geotag

DEF-hash.content:
A record's **hash** is a digest of its exact bytes — of a numbered record, or of the configuration. Unqualified, *hash*
means this.
DEF-hash.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-hash.title: A hash

DEF-library.content:
The **library** is the permanent, curated collection the media ends in — outside every workspace, and written only by
merge.
DEF-library.title: The library

DEF-managed_folders.title: The managed folders

DEF-merge.content:
**Merge**, the third phase, runs after a workspace has been geotagged and finalized: it moves the finalized media,
sorted by destination, into the library — never renaming or overwriting anything already there — and then seals the
workspace.
DEF-merge.title: Merge

DEF-operator_loop.content:
The **operator loop** is how the user drives the three phases through one workspace's life: prep organizes a dump; the
user sorts photos into photos by destination; prep records the sort; geotag is re-run, the user deciding what it asks,
until its plan is ready, and executes it; more dumps may follow, each from prep again; finalize closes the workspace's
record; merge moves it into the library. Each phase's own loop is in its own spec; this is the sequence across them.
DEF-operator_loop.title: The operator loop

DEF-prep.content:
**Prep**, the first phase, takes an unorganized dump and makes it a clean working set: it consolidates the dump,
normalizes extensions, sets duplicates aside (recoverably, never deleting), organizes the media by date, and hands
geotag what it found.
DEF-prep.title: Prep

DEF-sealed_workspace.content: A workspace is **sealed** once merge has succeeded in it: marked as finished, by a mark only merge writes.
DEF-sealed_workspace.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
DEF-sealed_workspace.title: A sealed workspace

DEF-strays_folder.content:
The **strays folder** is a media-tree folder at the workspace's top level. It holds the files that are not media which
prep moved out of the inbox, one subfolder for each run, their structure kept. It is neither a control record nor any
phase's output.
DEF-strays_folder.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
DEF-strays_folder.title: The strays folder

DEF-timestamp_name.content:
A file's **timestamp name** is the name prep and geotag give it from its timestamp, in the one format the configuration
sets, followed by a differentiating suffix when that name is taken.
DEF-timestamp_name.title: A timestamp name

DEF-tracks.content:
A workspace's **tracks** are the recorded position logs geotag reads as evidence: to propose time anchors, and to place
photos along them by interpolation or extrapolation. The configuration says where they are.
DEF-tracks.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
DEF-tracks.title: The tracks

DEF-transformation_log.content:
The **transformation log** is the human-readable account, photo by photo and keyed by each photo's fingerprint, of
everything done to it and why. Each phase keeps its own, carrying the previous phase's forward.
DEF-transformation_log.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-transformation_log.title: The transformation log

DEF-workspace.content:
A **workspace** is the transient place one ingest happens in: a dump of media enters it, the phases work on it in
turn, and merge empties it into the library. Every run acts on exactly one workspace.
DEF-workspace.title: The workspace

DEF-workspace_database.content:
The **workspace database** is the one database of record: what cartographer knows about the workspace's media — each
file's identity and metadata, what each phase derived from them, the values a photo held before geotag first changed
it, and the fingerprints of library files merge has read.
DEF-workspace_database.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-workspace_database.title: The workspace database

FCT-clocks_drift.content:
Each body's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes between days (drift, manual resets to local time
in the morning, missed DST). There is no single global offset to find.

*Where one has met it:* The import that landed an hour early; the shots an hour off after a border; a day's frames
scattered because the clock was never set — blamed on negligence or forgetfulness, not on a category.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-clocks_drift.title: Camera clocks drift — independently, and from day to day

FCT-large_batches.content:
A trip dump or a years-deep library is big and mixed: many RAW/JPEG frames across multiple cameras and phones.

*Where one has met it:* The card one keeps meaning to deal with; the decade of folders; or *"I'll geotag these
someday."*
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-large_batches.title: A photo batch is large — thousands of frames, several cameras

FCT-partial_track_coverage.content:
The logger's tracks reach *some* of the library, never all of it — so the track alone can never place every frame; the
rest needs fallbacks.

*Where one has met it:* The half-tagged library; the map view with holes where phone-sync missed; the frames that came
with a pin and the many that didn't.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-partial_track_coverage.title: GPX coverage is partial

INV-change_only_what_needs.content:
Every phase SHALL change only what its inputs actually require, as far as the work allows: no phase SHALL redo settled
work to be safe, and none SHALL leave a file in a state other than its inputs require.
INV-change_only_what_needs.title: A run changes only what its inputs require

INV-every_change_from_the_record.content:
Every change a phase makes SHALL follow from a decision the user recorded, or from a fixed rule applied to recorded
inputs — never from a choice the tool makes on its own. An execution SHALL act only on a plan made from those.
INV-every_change_from_the_record.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
INV-every_change_from_the_record.title: Every change follows from the record

INV-no_stale_use.content:
No phase SHALL use a record once anything it was derived from has changed. Each phase SHALL validate what it derives
from, then create the record, record those dependencies in it, and refuse its use downstream when any of them has
changed.
INV-no_stale_use.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
INV-no_stale_use.title: No record is used once what it came from has changed

INV-one_run_at_a_time.content:
At most one cartographer run SHALL act on a workspace at any time — whatever the commands: two runs of one phase, runs
of two phases, a merge, a finalize, or a quarantine prune.
INV-one_run_at_a_time.title: One run at a time

INV-undisturbed_shape.content:
No phase SHALL process an initialized workspace whose shape was disturbed from outside cartographer — an entry at its
top level that does not belong there, a symbolic link among its files, a managed folder missing — without stopping.
INV-undisturbed_shape.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
INV-undisturbed_shape.title: A disturbed workspace is never processed silently

RAT-a_link_escapes_the_tree.content:
Following a symbolic link would let a planned read or write reach a target **outside** the managed tree — a pipeline
escape that breaks the no-clobber and "originals never lost" guarantees and the closed-world assumption the content
fingerprint and de-duplication rest on.
RAT-a_link_escapes_the_tree.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-a_link_escapes_the_tree.title: A followed link escapes the managed tree

RAT-bare_first.content:
Bare-first is what makes an uncorrected file's provisional (prep) and final (geotag) names coincide, so geotag plans no
needless rename; the two phases use the identical rule so they never disagree on a name.
RAT-bare_first.title: The first free name makes the two names coincide

RAT-camera_groups_generated.content: **Camera groups are generated for the user**, ready to paste — leaving only the judgment, not the derivation.
RAT-camera_groups_generated.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-camera_groups_generated.title: The tedious part of a judgment call should be pre-computed

RAT-clustering_details.content:
**The consensus-clustering details** of clock-offset inference — clustering rather than averaging is forced by
robustness, but the spread thresholds, the tie-breaks, and the confidence grades are choices.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-clustering_details.title: The consensus-clustering details

RAT-coarse_trigger_for_the_cheap_plan.content:
The whole-file fingerprint restaling the plan is a catch-all guaranteeing no config-driven change is ever silently
missed, even one in an area without its own field-scoped fingerprint. It is intentional belt-and-braces *alongside* the
field-scoped fingerprints, not a contradiction of surgical staleness: they keep the **expensive** derived caches from
restaling on unrelated edits, while the **cheap-to-rebuild** plan simply re-plans on any config change. What surgical
staleness rules out is collapsing the *surgical* caches onto the whole-file hash; using that hash as an additional
coarse trigger for a cheap artifact is consistent with — indeed protective of — surgical staleness.
RAT-coarse_trigger_for_the_cheap_plan.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-coarse_trigger_for_the_cheap_plan.title: A coarse trigger for the cheap plan, a precise one for the costly caches

RAT-config_is_a_file.content:
Making the config a file binds it intrinsically to the workspace and to everything processed in it. Hashed and folded
into the dependency cascade, it closes the gap where an ambient config could change a run without leaving a trace; and
archived, it lets a future reader know not only what was decided but **under what configuration**.
RAT-config_is_a_file.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-config_is_a_file.title: A configuration in a file is bound to what it governed

RAT-configurable_folder_names.content:
**Defaults that are offered, not imposed.** Folder names (`0-sources … 6-photos-by-dest`) are configurable, not
hardcoded — the seven-stage *structure* is the invariant, the *labels* are the operator's. The rigidity is structural
where it must be and accommodating where it can afford to be.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-configurable_folder_names.title: Defaults that are offered, not imposed

RAT-consolidated_log.content:
A **consolidated, self-describing log in one kept folder** — *traceability arrived at, not chosen* (and it is this
traceability that lets the provenance tag above mean anything).
RAT-consolidated_log.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-consolidated_log.title: A choice made weeks earlier must still explain itself on return

RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.content:
Completeness means precision now *varies* across the library — so each placement must declare how trustworthy it is
(via the **traceability** the multi-session reality forces — see below).

**Every coordinate carries its derivation method** — native / GPX direct-match / interpolated / extrapolated / manual
— so a rough pin is never mistaken for a precise one.

*Why it is kept:* "I still want to be able to know, at a later date, how that GPS position was assigned - maybe I want
to refine it by image/place recognition for example." A new track needs no tag: it changes the GPX folder, which makes
the GPS decisions stale, and they are regenerated.

*The traceability:* "every decision must be traced, and by incorporating the precision, I allow it even in the final
library."
RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.title: Completeness means precision now *varies* across the library

RAT-database_is_record.content:
The database is not only a cache that makes re-runs cheap: it holds what nothing else does — the values a photo held
before geotag first changed it, which let any change be undone, and each photo's identity across its moves. Discarded
with the workspace, that knowledge would be lost; kept in two places, the two could disagree. The library keeps no
database because it is the user's own collection, organised as they choose, and merge only adds to it.
RAT-database_is_record.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-database_is_record.title: The database holds what the record cannot rebuild

RAT-database_shows_only_now.content:
The live database is one file that every phase changes, so at any moment it shows only the latest state: what prep
knew is overwritten by what geotag learned. An image taken at each phase's end keeps the database's state at every
boundary, to be opened later and compared.
RAT-database_shows_only_now.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-database_shows_only_now.title: A database shows only now

RAT-decision_withdrawable.content:
An **original-values ledger** keeps what each photo held before the tool first changed it, and every plan decides from
it, so deleting a decision *restores* the prior state.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decision_withdrawable.title: A decision must be withdrawable

RAT-decisions_cascade.content:
Decisions **cascade**: *one far-reaching choice high in the tree is traded for many short-reaching ones* — inherit
unless overridden, remembered across re-runs. (This is where "far-reaching" comes from — a chosen trade, not an
inherent property.)
RAT-decisions_cascade.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decisions_cascade.title: Asking per-photo would be thousands of short-reaching chores

RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.content:
Decisions are **idempotently re-read each run**; the fast store is **SQLite as a cache only** — derived, rebuildable,
never the source of truth.
RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.title: Resuming must not mean re-deciding

RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.content: A **decoded-pixel fingerprint** (ImageMagick/ffmpeg), not file bytes, as each photo's stable identity.
RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.title: Identity must survive EXIF rewrites and renames

RAT-derivation_version_is_code.content:
The version of the camera-group derivation takes part in the dependency fingerprints, so a change to the derivation is
detectable; it versions the code that computes the key, so only the code can set it.
RAT-derivation_version_is_code.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-derivation_version_is_code.title: The derivation's version must stay the code's

RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.content:
The destination tree must be a **hierarchy** — the cascade rides on folder nesting, so a flat or tag-based layout can't
inherit at all, and every value would fall back to per-photo entry.
RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.title: Inheritance needs an axis to travel along

RAT-development_after_corrections.content:
Distribution copies made before geotag's time and position corrections would be made from uncorrected photos, and the
corrections would invalidate them. Nor is the workspace a place for processing image files at all: that work belongs
to the library. A development folder's presence alone is the signal; nothing guesses whether it really holds output.
RAT-development_after_corrections.title: Corrections would invalidate development

RAT-discrete_stages.content:
**Discrete, inspectable stages** (the numbered pipeline) — each a real checkpoint; the **filesystem is treated as
truth**.
RAT-discrete_stages.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-discrete_stages.title: A crash must be recoverable

RAT-dry_run_reads_the_saved_plan.content: Because the full plan is a persisted artifact, the dry run reports on the on-disk plan — still not a simulation.
RAT-dry_run_reads_the_saved_plan.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-dry_run_reads_the_saved_plan.title: The dry run reads the persisted plan

RAT-durable_record.content:
That, in turn, forces the record machinery — and note what is *not* a driver here: auditability and decade-longevity,
are **zero-cost benefits** that fall out of building for resumability.
RAT-durable_record.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-durable_record.title: Durable, resumable record

RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.content: The editor writes **only the `user_decision` field** — never derived or evidence fields.
RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.title: The record must stay an honest statement of *intent*, not a mutable scratchpad

RAT-finalize_apart.content:
Geotag is re-run freely, and assembling the permanent record on each pass would be wasted work. Finalize marks the one
moment the user declares the dump done.
RAT-finalize_apart.title: Finalize stays apart because geotag is re-run

RAT-fingerprint_and_hash_opposite_jobs.content:
The two words name a value by the role it plays, not by the algorithm underneath, and the two roles are opposite: one
must be invariant under mutation, the other sensitive to it. They keep different names even though a fingerprint is
itself computed with a hash function.
RAT-fingerprint_and_hash_opposite_jobs.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-fingerprint_and_hash_opposite_jobs.title: Opposite jobs, so different names

RAT-folder_gps_fallback.content:
A **cascading folder-level GPS fallback** — set one coordinate at a trip's root and it is inherited down the tree (P3
makes this cheap; one answer covers many photos).
RAT-folder_gps_fallback.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-folder_gps_fallback.title: Placement cannot depend on the track alone

RAT-folder_roles_are_logic.content:
The roles — the inbox, the read-only destination tree, the order in which duplicates are retained, which folders are
the photo and video bands — are pipeline logic, so the user sets the names and never the roles.
RAT-folder_roles_are_logic.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-folder_roles_are_logic.title: A folder's role is pipeline logic

RAT-format_editor_split.content: **Format + editor split**: JSON is the record; the Time/Drift/GPS app is what writes it.
RAT-format_editor_split.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-format_editor_split.title: Intricate, evidence-specific decisions are too error-prone to hand-edit

RAT-gates_not_history.content:
What bounds geotag's freedom is a small, fixed set of conditions on the workspace, not a "has geotag run before?" flag.
Each gate names a state geotag cannot work correctly from; none says anything about history.
RAT-gates_not_history.title: Bounded by what is true now, not by a flag

RAT-grouping_computed_once.content:
One derived key identifies a camera or device so that grouping is computed once, by prep, and reused by geotag — never
reinvented.
RAT-grouping_computed_once.title: Grouping computed once is never reinvented

RAT-handoff_by_content.content:
Living in the skipped directory is independent of the handoff's role as a dependency: it is invisible to prep's media
scan yet fully verified as a dependency by geotag — verified by content, not by exact bytes, so a run-only refresh of
it does not restale downstream.
RAT-handoff_by_content.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-handoff_by_content.title: The handoff is invisible to the scan, yet verified

RAT-hash_is_for_change.content:
A hash is chosen precisely so it changes on any byte change: detecting change is its whole purpose, which is what makes
it the right dependency check for records.
RAT-hash_is_for_change.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-hash_is_for_change.title: Detecting change is a hash's whole purpose

RAT-idempotent_reruns.content: **Idempotent, diff-based** re-runs; a run over unchanged state is a no-op.
RAT-idempotent_reruns.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-idempotent_reruns.title: Re-runs must not redo settled work or cause churn

RAT-identity_survives_edits.content:
A fingerprint is chosen precisely so it stays the same when the pipeline rewrites a photo's metadata or position or
renames the file: a media file's identity must survive those mutations, which is what makes it the identity spine the
transformation log and de-duplication rely on.
RAT-identity_survives_edits.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-identity_survives_edits.title: A file's identity outlives its edits

RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.content:
Never overwriting guards photos, which cannot be made again. An image can: it is a copy of the live database, and only
the latest end of each phase is worth keeping, so a phase's next successful run replaces its image — whole, so that a
capture interrupted leaves a usable image either way.
RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.title: An image is regenerable; a photo is not

RAT-library_is_ground_truth.content:
The library is the user's curated collection: its organisation and names are the ground truth, and other tools and
people rely on them. So merge adds to it and changes nothing in it, and assumes it is in order rather than scanning it:
scanning a whole library to place one batch would cost far more than it saves. Where a name is taken, only the content
tells a copy already present from a different photo sharing a name.
RAT-library_is_ground_truth.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_is_ground_truth.title: The library is the user's, and already in order

RAT-library_reads_cost.content:
Fingerprinting a library file means reading and decoding it whole, and the library may sit across a network. Kept in the workspace, a
fingerprint already taken spares that read on the next run, and stays right while the file is unchanged.
RAT-library_reads_cost.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_reads_cost.title: A library file costs a full read

RAT-linux_and_open_source_not_roots.content:
This is built and run on Linux, but Linux is not a root — the design is plain Python shelling out to `exiftool`,
ImageMagick, and `ffmpeg`, all cross-platform, so it would port with little structural change. Open-source is likewise
a downstream expression of the "local, owned" ethos (P1, P2), not a structural driver. Neither forces anything below.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-linux_and_open_source_not_roots.title: Linux and open-source are not roots

RAT-lock_and_revalidation.content:
This whole-run lock is independent of, and stricter than, the dependency-revalidation discipline: revalidation guards
against *stale* inputs across separate runs, while the lock guarantees runs never overlap in the first place.
RAT-lock_and_revalidation.title: The lock and revalidation guard different things

RAT-longevity_is_free.content: *(zero-cost benefit)* Decade-longevity and "open one folder years later" come free — incidental, never the driver.
RAT-longevity_is_free.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-longevity_is_free.title: Built to survive a three-week gap, it survives a thirty-year one

RAT-loop_is_steady_state.content:
The loop is a steady state to return to, not a one-way pipeline: a batch can be imported, sorted, and followed by
another before anything is geotagged. A phase that judged by what ran before would have to forbid that; one that judges
the present state need not.
RAT-loop_is_steady_state.title: A steady state to return to

RAT-mark_in_the_file.content:
What geotag did to a photo is marked in the photo itself rather than kept only in the workspace: the mark survives the
workspace, reaches the library, and is read back wherever the photo turns up again, so a photo corrected once is
recognised as corrected whichever workspace it is in.
RAT-mark_in_the_file.title: The file carries the record of what geotag did

RAT-merge_appends.content:
Merge appends at `max+1` rather than reusing a freed-up lower number because the library is append-only and a re-run
must reproduce the same name.
RAT-merge_appends.title: The library is append-only

RAT-merge_never_half_done.content:
Finalize is a point in time, and photos by destination can change after it. Merge checks the finalized set against the
present one rather than trusting finalize was last, so a half-geotagged set cannot reach the library.
RAT-merge_never_half_done.title: Never a half-geotagged set in the library

RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.content:
Such intricacy would be brutal to enter by hand, so P3 (ask only what the data can't settle) governs how it is
collected — and introduces the document's central trade.
RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.title: Minimal, cascading asks

RAT-move_not_copy.content:
A copy left in the workspace of a photo already in the library is a duplicate that invites confusion and wastes space,
so merge moves rather than copies, and removes a copy whose content the library already holds. What stays behind is
exactly what still needs attention. Removing the workspace's copy last, once the library's is verified, means an
interruption never loses a photo: running merge again finishes the work.
RAT-move_not_copy.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-move_not_copy.title: The workspace keeps only what still needs attention

RAT-multi_session_job.content:
This is a **two-level chain**: a fact and a choice together force an intermediate consequence, and that consequence
forces the record machinery. It is the part most easily mistaken for an arbitrary choice.

Neither root does it alone. Scale (F1) without the 100%-coverage goal (P4) is fast: prep is automated, one keeps the
native-GPS frames, lets the track cover the easy matches, and stops — plausibly one sitting, because the long tail is
never chased. The goal without scale is also trivial: placing ten photos completely takes minutes. Only *total
coverage across a large, mixed batch* produces a long tail of per-(camera, destination, day) offset confirmations and
hand-placed remainder that cannot be finished in one sitting.

Note: not all of that elapsed time is P4's. The album **sort** into a destination tree is owed to **P2** — one would
drag photos into folders even with no geotagging at all — so P2 contributes session-spanning human time on its own.
What F1 + P4 *specifically* add is the **long tail of confirmations and manual placement** that has no automated
escape. Either way, the job likely spans multiple sessions.

**Intermediate consequence — a multi-session job.** The machine cannot hold one's decisions in its head between
sittings.
RAT-multi_session_job.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-multi_session_job.title: A multi-session job

RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.content:
A photo is renamed up to twice in the workspace — a provisional name, then its final one — and may be renamed again on
its way into the library, so no name identifies it across its journey. Its fingerprint does: it survives every rename,
move and metadata write the pipeline makes.
RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.title: A name cannot key the log

RAT-never_behind_prep.content:
Geotag depends on prep's handoff, and a photo prep has not recorded is not in it. Re-prepping after every sort, even
after geotag has run, keeps the handoff the whole truth about photos by destination.
RAT-never_behind_prep.title: New photos never reach geotag behind prep's back

RAT-no_automatic_deletion.content: Duplicates are **quarantined**, never removed; pruning is an explicit, separate act.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-no_automatic_deletion.title: Deletion is never automatic

RAT-no_hidden_litter.content: Hidden dotfiles are swept to the recoverable quarantine, not merely skipped, so a dump leaves no hidden litter.
RAT-no_hidden_litter.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-no_hidden_litter.title: A dump leaves no hidden litter

RAT-no_mutation_outside_plan.content: **plan → validate → execute**; the dry-run *is* the serialized plan; stale plans are rejected against current state.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-no_mutation_outside_plan.title: No mutation outside a validated plan

RAT-no_redo_to_be_safe.content:
Settled work done again "to be safe" makes nothing safer: a file written with what it already holds gains nothing and
risks a failed write, and reading a library's content again can cost hours.
RAT-no_redo_to_be_safe.title: Redoing settled work buys no safety

RAT-non_destructive_core.content: plan / validate / execute; atomic no-clobber; quarantine, not delete; original-values ledger.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-non_destructive_core.title: Non-destructive core

RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.content:
Start with the fact. Because each camera's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes from day to day
(F2), there is no single offset to discover — the correct answer is **per (camera group, destination, day)**. *That*
granularity is the entire source of the decisions' "complexity": it is a consequence of real, time-varying drift, not a
premise.

The offset is **inferred and applied per (camera group, destination, day)**; corrections fall *between* destinations,
never within one — which is why **one destination = one coherent shoot**.
RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.title: Drift is per-camera and per-day, so no global offset is correct

RAT-one_authorship_principle.content: The three phases share one stance on authorship, stated once; each phase states only how it meets it.
RAT-one_authorship_principle.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-one_authorship_principle.title: One principle, stated once

RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.content:
The mechanism is named for ZFS because that is the reference implementation, but it is deliberately the *only* part
of the pipeline that touches a specific filesystem feature, and it is optional; everything else is filesystem-agnostic.
RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.title: Why the snapshot alone may touch the filesystem

RAT-one_format_no_drift.content:
With one format key for the whole pipeline, the provisional names prep assigns and the final names geotag assigns are
guaranteed to share the same textual shape and can never drift apart; there is no format divergence to reconcile.
RAT-one_format_no_drift.title: One key, so the names cannot drift apart

RAT-one_idempotency_principle.content:
The three phases share one sense of idempotency, stated once for all of them; each phase states only what it means in
its own terms, so the principle cannot drift between them.
RAT-one_idempotency_principle.title: One principle, stated once

RAT-one_skipped_place.content:
Skipping the control directory wholesale means a control or artifact file can never be mistaken for a photo. There is
no per-file "ignore list" to maintain — consolidating everything in one skipped directory replaces the basename
registry that earlier designs needed.
RAT-one_skipped_place.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-one_skipped_place.title: One skipped place instead of a list of names

RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.content: Each phase that mutates uses the same mechanism so the phases behave identically and cannot diverge.
RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One mechanism, so the phases cannot diverge

RAT-one_source_per_fact.content:
The facts the dependencies are built from — the configuration, the control records, the camera-group derivation's
version, the filename format, the tracks, the snapshot mechanism — are each defined once, for every phase, so that a
single change has one authoritative source and a predictable staleness footprint everywhere.
RAT-one_source_per_fact.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-one_source_per_fact.title: One source for each shared fact

RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.content:
Geotag's and merge's plans locate the destination tree by name and classify the tree, and renaming a managed folder or
moving an extension between media and `other` changes which files exist where. Prep re-plans from the filesystem each
run and guards execution with the whole-file hash, so it needs no separate folder or extension fingerprint of its own.
RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.title: Folder names and media classes decide which files exist where

RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.content:
The structural facts are shared by every phase because each relies on them when it scans, and a violation of any one
means the workspace was disturbed out-of-band. The guards compose with — but are distinct from — input validation, which
checks *authored values*, and the dependency cascade, which checks *change*: these check the *shape of the workspace
itself*.
RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.title: Every phase relies on the shape when it scans

RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.content:
Timezone, clock offset, and GPS fallback are **piggybacked on the destination sort** one would do anyway for real albums
(P2).
RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.title: The unavoidable human act should pay for itself

RAT-plain_json_record.content: **Plain JSON** decision artifacts — the durable external record, read back at the start of each session.
RAT-plain_json_record.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-plain_json_record.title: Decisions can't live in the tool between sessions, so they must persist outside it

RAT-planning_inside_lock.content:
Planning is non-mutating, but it must still not run concurrently: a plan computed against a workspace another process
is reading or mutating is untrustworthy, so planning is inside the lock too.
RAT-planning_inside_lock.title: A plan made beside another run cannot be trusted

RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.content:
The destination tree is read-only for prep yet still scanned by it, so prep is also the gatekeeper for links that
appear there; and the mandatory re-prep after any change to it means geotag and merge only ever consume a handoff prep
built with no forbidden link present.
RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.title: Prep is the gatekeeper for links under the destination tree

RAT-prune_harms_nothing.content:
The quarantine holds only spare copies of duplicates, which a sealed workspace still keeps. Deleting them touches no
photo, library file, record or row of the database, and neither reprocesses the workspace nor adds a batch to it, so
the seal's reasons do not reach it, and the space can be reclaimed.
RAT-prune_harms_nothing.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-prune_harms_nothing.title: Pruning the quarantine changes nothing controlled

RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.content:
Since prep creates the structure once and never removes a folder, a missing one is evidence the structure was deleted
or moved out-of-band — not a state any phase produces. Silently rebuilding it could mask a real loss: a deleted folder
may have taken organized media with it. Recovering lost media — from an optional pre-mutation snapshot, say — is the
operator's task.
RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.title: A rebuilt structure could mask a loss

RAT-record_outlives_workspace.content:
The decisions drive a run, but their lasting value is as the record of what was done to the archive and why — and the
workspace is transient: it is merged and set aside, or set aside at any phase boundary without ever advancing. Decisions
are kept for the future only if preserved beyond it, in one known place, rather than scattered in per-file sidecars or,
as with tools that change files and forget, not recorded at all. Since a workspace may stop at any phase, the record
must be whole at each.
RAT-record_outlives_workspace.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-record_outlives_workspace.title: The workspace is transient; the record must not be

RAT-records_attributable.content:
With each phase writing only its own records and carrying earlier ones forward by copy, every phase's output stays a
stable record attributable to it, which no later phase can silently change: complete at its boundary, and evident if
tampered with by what came after. That is why the log is three files, one per phase, not one changed in place. And a
phase that copies its predecessor's record, rather than deriving that history again from other sources, keeps one
account of each phase: a second, rebuilt account could disagree with the first.
RAT-records_attributable.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-records_attributable.title: A record no later phase can silently alter

RAT-recoverable_core.content:
Crash-recovery follows from P1 (an interrupted run must never strand an original half-changed); the diff-based
idempotency also answers F3 — because coverage is partial, one adds more tracks or photos later and re-runs, so a run
must act only on what actually changed.
RAT-recoverable_core.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-recoverable_core.title: Recoverable core

RAT-remainder_worklist.content:
An explicit, short **remainder worklist** — what no evidence can locate is collected for a manual pin, not left off the
map.
RAT-remainder_worklist.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-remainder_worklist.title: The true unplaceable set must be surfaced, never silently dropped

RAT-rerun_is_safe.content:
Geotag can be re-run freely because a re-run redoes nothing settled: the user's decisions live in geotag's records and
survive their regeneration, what geotag wrote into a file is recognised there, so a corrected time is never corrected
twice and photos added later are corrected beside it, and a name computed from the destination's local time comes out
the same.
RAT-rerun_is_safe.title: Re-running is safe because nothing settled is redone

RAT-rerun_not_frictionless.content:
"Freely re-runnable" does not mean "always a no-op". Any change upstream — not only new media — restales exactly what
depends on it, and may raise new questions about the items it touches; a re-run does that work and no more.
RAT-rerun_not_frictionless.title: Safe is not frictionless

RAT-reseal_automatic.content:
Merge adds to the record finalize packaged, so that package no longer describes the whole journey. Since merge is the
workspace's last act, remaking the package once at its end is what the user always wants. Finalize stays its own
command because geotag is freely re-run, and re-packaging after every pass would be wasted.
RAT-reseal_automatic.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-reseal_automatic.title: Merge is the end, so the package is remade at once

RAT-retention_serves_the_log.content:
A journey spans many runs — prep, re-prep after moves, repeated geotag passes, merge — so a log rebuilt from the last
run alone would silently lose the rest. What is kept exists to serve the log, and resuming and auditing; it is not an
open-ended store of events.
RAT-retention_serves_the_log.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-retention_serves_the_log.title: Retention serves the log, nothing more

RAT-safety_not_on_the_plan.content: No-clobber **re-verified atomically at the moment of each write**, not just at plan time.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-safety_not_on_the_plan.title: Safety cannot rest on the plan being correct

RAT-same_shape_different_value.content:
Both phases use the same format, but the **value** differs by phase and that difference is intentional. Because the
shape is identical, a file's name changes between phases only when its timestamp is genuinely corrected; an uncorrected
file's provisional and final names coincide, so geotag plans no needless rename for it.
RAT-same_shape_different_value.title: The same shape, a different value, on purpose

RAT-seal_not_folder_state.content:
Photos by destination is empty both in a workspace just sorted and in one merged and finished, so its state cannot say
which a workspace is. A mark written only when merge succeeds whole can — and a merge that left a photo behind writes
none, so it can be finished by running it again.
RAT-seal_not_folder_state.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-seal_not_folder_state.title: An empty folder means two things; a mark means one

RAT-sealed_is_final.content:
A second batch processed in a merged workspace would interleave with the first's database, logs and package, and its
record would no longer describe one dump. So nothing that could change it runs; the records stay readable; and a dump
dropped there is left untouched and pointed out, for the user to move to a fresh workspace by hand — safer than any
automated move inside a finished workspace.
RAT-sealed_is_final.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-sealed_is_final.title: A finished workspace is read, not reprocessed

RAT-snapshot_is_extra.content:
**Snapshots are an optional extra safety layer, not a requirement.** The pipeline operates fully and safely without
them: correctness and recoverability rest on the journal, recoverable quarantine, no-clobber operations, and
filesystem-as-truth reconciliation. Snapshots add a clean-slate rollback path on top of those for operators whose
filesystem supports it; they are not the basis of the safety model.
RAT-snapshot_is_extra.title: A snapshot is an extra layer, not the safety model

RAT-stage_cut_points.content:
**The exact decomposition into seven stages** rather than six or eight. The *principle* of discrete inspectable
checkpoints is forced (P1+F3); the specific cut points are judgment.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-stage_cut_points.title: The exact decomposition into stages

RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.content:
Setting the prior artifact aside keeps a superseded plan and any authored decisions recoverable; writing nothing on an
unchanged re-run means the iterative decision-editing loop does not accumulate redundant backups.
RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.title: A superseded plan stays recoverable; an unchanged one adds nothing

RAT-surgical_staleness.content:
Collapsing all staleness to a single whole-file hash would needlessly restale unrelated artifacts on any edit, and is
explicitly not done.
RAT-surgical_staleness.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-surgical_staleness.title: Surgical staleness: one hash for everything would restale everything

RAT-time_name_recomputed.content:
A file's time and name are not rolled back when a decision is withdrawn but recomputed in place: reverting them would
un-position a file the user has already organized.
RAT-time_name_recomputed.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-time_name_recomputed.title: A time and a name are recomputed, not reverted

RAT-total_coverage_cascade.content:
This choice fights F3: tracks cover only *part* of the library, but the output must be *whole*. That gap is what forces
the fallback machinery to exist: without P4, tracks alone would be the entire story and everything below would be
unnecessary.
RAT-total_coverage_cascade.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-total_coverage_cascade.title: Total-coverage cascade

RAT-track_squeezed.content:
**Direct match → interpolation between points → bounded extrapolation off the ends**, each used before falling back to
manual.
RAT-track_squeezed.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-track_squeezed.title: Every placeable point of the track must be squeezed out

RAT-tracks_kept_outside.content:
The shared rule that makes it safe for geotag alone to own the tracks is where they live. Kept outside the managed
folders, prep's normal scan never encounters them, so they can never be taken for files of no media class, or swept
into the inbox and organized.
RAT-tracks_kept_outside.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_kept_outside.title: Where the tracks live is what keeps them geotag's

RAT-tracks_never_strays.content:
Parked among the strays, a track could be deleted when the strays are cleared in bulk, and a lost track is evidence no
re-run can recover. Refusing to run leaves it where the user put it until they move it to the tracks' location.
RAT-tracks_never_strays.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_never_strays.title: A track among the strays could be deleted with them

RAT-which_folder_library.content:
**The downstream library, not the tree.** A *hierarchical* destination tree is **forced**, not chosen: the timezone /
offset / GPS-fallback cascade rides on the folder nesting, so a flat or tag-based layout would make inheritance
impossible and drive the per-photo workload straight back up. What is actually free is only *which* folder-based
library consumes the result — digiKam, or any other — and the cosmetic naming of the levels.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-which_folder_library.title: The downstream library, not the tree

RAT-why_did_this_change.content:
For irreplaceable photos, a user who distrusts opaque, automatic change must always be able to answer *why did this
change happen?* — and to change the answer. So the tool proposes and the user decides, the decision stays in a durable
record that the change can be traced back to, and revising the record revises the result.
RAT-why_did_this_change.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-why_did_this_change.title: A user who distrusts opaque mutation can always ask why

RAT-workspace_not_recycled.content:
Even with photos by destination empty, a merged workspace keeps its database, ledgers, caches, snapshots and sealed
record. Starting afresh keeps each workspace's record about one batch.
RAT-workspace_not_recycled.title: A merged workspace is not a clean slate

RUL-any_config_change_replans.content:
Any change to the configuration, in whatever area, SHALL make stale every plan made before it — prep's plan, geotag's
executable plan and merge's plan — and none of them SHALL be executed.
RUL-any_config_change_replans.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RUL-any_config_change_replans.title: Any configuration change restales the plan

RUL-camera_classes_not_derivation.content:
The configuration SHALL say which camera groups are phones and which have fixed clocks — the only part of camera
grouping it sets. How a camera group is derived, and the version of that derivation, SHALL NOT be configurable.
RUL-camera_classes_not_derivation.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RUL-camera_classes_not_derivation.title: The user classifies camera groups; how they are derived is fixed

RUL-camera_group_derivation_versioned.content:
How camera groups are derived SHALL carry a version, which SHALL take part in the checks of freshness and of
dependencies, so that a change to the derivation is detected and old and new groups are never silently mixed.
RUL-camera_group_derivation_versioned.title: The derivation carries a version

RUL-carry_forward_by_copy.content:
To carry an earlier phase's record forward, a phase SHALL copy it to a record of its own and extend the copy, leaving
the earlier one untouched; it SHALL NOT derive an earlier phase's history again.
RUL-carry_forward_by_copy.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RUL-carry_forward_by_copy.title: An earlier record is carried forward by copying it

RUL-cause_locatable.content:
Every change a phase executes SHALL be traceable in the records, from the decision and the inputs it was made from,
through the plan, to the record of what ran — so a wrong result points at a recorded choice.
RUL-cause_locatable.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RUL-cause_locatable.title: The cause of every change can be found

RUL-collision_by_content.content:
Where an incoming photo's place in the library is taken, merge SHALL compare the two by fingerprint. The same content
SHALL mean the photo is already in the library: nothing is written there, and the workspace's copy is removed. Different
content SHALL mean two photos share a name: the incoming one is placed under a differentiating name.
RUL-collision_by_content.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RUL-collision_by_content.title: A taken place is settled by content

RUL-config_archived.content: The configuration SHALL be part of the archival record the workspace leaves behind.
RUL-config_archived.omit_reason: carried by the archival package's items, when §13 of the shared contract is converted
RUL-config_archived.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RUL-config_archived.title: The configuration is part of the permanent record

RUL-config_authoritative.content:
The seed defaults SHALL serve only to seed a new workspace. Once a workspace's configuration exists, it SHALL govern
